ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+3$ ($a\neq 0$) intersects the x-axis at points $A(1,0)$ and $B(-3,0)$ and intersects the y-axis at point $C$. Connect $BC$ and intersect the axis of symmetry of the parabola at point $E$, with the vertex being point $D$. What is the equation of the parabola?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the parabola $y=ax^{2}+bx+3$ ($a\neq 0$) intersects the x-axis at points A $(1,0)$ and B $(-3,0)$,\\
it follows that $\begin{cases} a+b+3=0 \\ 9a-3b+3=0 \end{cases}$,\\
solving these equations yields $\begin{cases} a=-1 \\ b=-2 \end{cases}$,\\
therefore, the equation of the parabola is $\boxed{y=-x^{2}-2x+3}$.
